narrative:
The model has analyzed your academic journey and determined that there’s a **39% chance** you might struggle to pass your final year. While this isn’t a guarantee of failure, it’s high enough that your school has decided you should take extra support courses to help you succeed. Think of it like a warning sign on a road—it’s not saying you *will* crash, but it’s telling you to slow down and pay extra attention.

The biggest factors pushing this prediction are three key areas. First, the model noticed that you spend **a lot of free time after school** and go out with friends **very little**, which might mean you’re not balancing your studies well. Most students who don’t need extra help have a more balanced mix of free time and focus. Second, the fact that you **haven’t had any past class failures** actually worked *against* this prediction—it suggests you’re capable of doing the work, but the model is still concerned about how you’re managing your time now. Finally, your **family relationships are rated as very good**, which usually helps students, but the model sees this as a smaller factor compared to your study habits.

The most critical issue is how you’re using your time outside of school. While you’re not skipping classes or struggling with health, the model is flagging that your current routine might not be setting you up for success. The extra courses aren’t a punishment—they’re a chance to adjust your approach, whether that means cutting back on distractions, finding a study schedule that works for you, or getting help with time management. This is your opportunity to turn things around before it’s too late.

Protected attributes sex, age and health were not used to make the machine prediction.
